key_insight: Circulating extracellular vesicle lipid profiles can distinguish ALS from healthy controls and spinal muscular atrophy, suggesting a disease-specific blood biomarker signal tied to membrane remodelling.
clinical_relevance: These EV lipid signatures may support ALS diagnosis, patient stratification, and treatment monitoring, including tracking response changes in tofersen-treated SOD1-ALS.
method: Mass spectrometry-based lipidomics of circulating extracellular vesicles
Multivariate modelling to classify ALS versus control and related neuromuscular diseases
Independent cohort validation and longitudinal comparison in treated patients
evidence_signal: ALS was separated from healthy controls with AUROC 0.90 in the main cohort, 0.92 when low-confidence predictions were withheld, and 0.78 in an independent cohort; SMA showed a distinct lipid fingerprint.
watch_item: Performance drops in external validation, so broader standardization and prospective multi-site testing are needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Circulating extracellular vesicle lipidomics identifies distinct signatures of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and spinal muscular atrophy
